rounds.text: The valuation of Supreme Power Equipment Ltd (SUPREMEPWR) appears undervalued when compared to its sector peers. The company trades at a P/E ratio of 24.8x [E1], which is significantly lower than the sector benchmark of 33.24x [E6]. This suggests that investors are not fully recognizing the company's earnings potential or may be undervaluing it relative to its competitors. Furthermore, the company’s Price-to-Book (P/B) ratio of 4.36x [E7] is also lower than the sector benchmark of 5.75x, indicating that the market might be underestimating the value of the firm's assets. The Return on Assets (ROA) stands at a robust 7.91% [E8], outperforming the sector by a wide margin, which implies efficient asset utilization and profitability. Cash conversion is another strong point for SUPREMEPWR, with an operating cash flow to reported profit ratio of 1.40x in March 2026 [E28]. This means that the company's profits are fully backed by cash, suggesting a healthy financial position and operational efficiency. Additionally, the operating cash flow was Rs 28 Cr in March 2026 [E30], while free cash flow was negative at -Rs 30 Cr [E31], but this is offset by the strong cash conversion ratio. In summary, these factors—lower P/E and P/B ratios compared to sector peers, higher ROA, and strong cash conversion—indicate that SUPREMEPWR may be undervalued in the market.
